text:
Ravi Gupta: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to lock the fallback semantics for billing events when token attribution arrives late or is missing.
Maya Chen: Are we still leaning toward two-tier events? audit-events (immutable) + billing-views (derived)?
Liam O'Connor: yes, audit-events + periodically computed aggregates. keeps replay simple and audit-friendly.
Anika Patel: Concern: audit-events store per-token entries -> huge volume. can we store only per-request deltas + compacted token counts?
Ravi Gupta: Tradeoff: per-request deltas lose token-level explainability for audits. We should keep per-token only for flagged requests (high-value/enterprise) and otherwise compact.
Jesse Park: For dedupe and replay we need deterministic event ids. Proposal: `sha256(customer_id + request_id + seq)` as `event_id`.
ingest-bot: ingest-bot: New schema committed to trunk: https://internal/docs/billing/pipeline-schema
Maya Chen: +1 on deterministic ids. Also add `original_timestamp` + `source_offset` so we can order late arrivals.
Liam O'Connor: For platform infra: Kafka with log compaction + consumer-driven materialized view; SQS won't support compaction easily.
Anika Patel: What about exactly-once? We can't guarantee; design for idempotence using event_id dedupe in storage layer.
Ravi Gupta: Agreed. Storage should expose `applyIfNotSeen(event_id)` semantics for billing aggregates.
Jesse Park: Fallbacks: if attribution missing after X minutes, compute best-effort attribution using sampling model estimates and mark `attribution_confidence: low`.
Maya Chen: Need policy: low-confidence attributions must be labeled and counted separately for audits, and trigger downstream alerts when matched to enterprise accounts.
Liam O'Connor: Implementation note: keep two retention tiers: 90 days full audit-events, 3 years compacted aggregates for invoicing.
Anika Patel: Also encrypt identifiers at rest and only store hashed conversation ids in audit-events. no raw prompts in billing pipeline.
Ravi Gupta: Replay plan: replay from audit-events; aggregates are deterministic if we use same reduction function. document the reducer and make it portable.
Jesse Park: Example event payload we'd store in audit-events (pseudocode):
```
{
  "event_id": "sha256(...)",
  "customer_id": "cust_123",
  "request_id": "req_456",
  "type": "token_attribution",
  "token_count": 42,
  "model": "gpt4-x",
  "timestamp": 1748001232,
  "attribution_confidence": "high"
}
```
Maya Chen: Ops question: SLA for billing pipeline ingestion? we need 99.5% within 2m for hosted tiers, 5m for Dedicated.
Liam O'Connor: We'll add backpressure: if consumer lag > threshold, route to cheap aggregator that emits per-request totals only.
Anika Patel: We should add an audit flag for `manually_adjusted` so we can trace charge corrections.
Ravi Gupta: Next actions: Maya to write a short PR with fallback rules, Jesse to add deterministic event id helper, Liam to draft infra plan with Kafka compaction and retention. Ping me when PRs are ready.
Maya Chen: will do, target EOD tomorrow :thumbsup:
Jesse Park: I'll add the helper and tests. 
Liam O'Connor: I'll sketch infra and post a diagram in #eng-architecture by Monday.
ingest-bot: ingest-bot: CI build passed for billing-schema branch :white_check_mark:
Ravi Gupta: Thanks team. If anyone sees compliance edge-cases speak up now. :thinking:
